To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the seismic properties of a detachment system can be calculated from the elastic stiffness tensors of individual minerals and the measured crystallographic preferred orientation (CPO); (b) the seismic properties are anisotropic and depend on the mineral composition of the rock and the orientation of the CPO of the minerals.
the seismic anisotropes of the rocks of the Aegean crust can be explained by the presence of aligned mica, glaucophane, quartz and calcite.

the seismic properties of rocks from the West Cycladic detachment system are strongly influenced by the crystallographic preferred orientation of the minerals and that the anisotropy has the same orientation as the extensional direction in the Aegea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the seismic properties of a crustal scale extensional detachment system.
the seismic anisotropy of the Aegean lithosphere.

the relationship between the seismic properties and the crystallographic preferred orientation of the rocks in the West Cycladic detachment system, Aeolian Islands, and the implications for the crustal anisotropes of the Aegean region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the seismic properties of a rock are strongly influenced by its mineralogy and crystallographic preferred orientation, with the latter being controlled by the deformational history of the rock.
the anisotropic properties of the Aegean crust are mainly controlled by the orientation of micas and the presence of glaucophane.

the Aegean region is a good example of a crust that has undergone extensional tectonics and that the anisotropic properties of the crust are strongly controlled by the mineral alignment that developed in response to the extension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seismic anisotropes of the Aegean crust are mainly caused by the preferred orientations of the mica minerals and to a lesser extent of calcite.
the CPOs of the minerals are the main control of the anisotropic seismic properties of the crustal rocks.

the CPOs of the minerals in the rocks are responsible for the seismic anisotropy of the Aegean crust, and that the anisotropic properties of the Aegeen crust are controlled by the orientation of the foliation and by the orientation of mica and glaucophane crystals in the rocks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anisotropic properties of rocks in the crustal scale detachment systems can be used to constrain their tectonic history and the deformational mechanisms that led to the formation of the system.
the CPO of the constituent minerals can be used to predict seismic anisotropy, and that the anisotropy can be used as a tool to infer the structural history of the rocks.
the seismic properties of a crustal scale shear zone are strongly controlled by mineral crystallographic orientation.
